messages:
maria (oncall): paging: I'm getting a bunch of alerts from the synthetic checks — latency on text-generation API up ~6x. Not seeing errors in hosted metrics yet. Can eng-sre take?

incident-bot: Paging — Sev2: High tail latency for /v1/generate (detected 1776504300). Routed to on-call: maria.

kevin (eng-sre): on it. is this isolated to a region? which models?

maria (oncall): eu-west1 only so far. Affects both small and large LLMs. Console shows normal request counts, but API response times spike.

olivia (eng-runtime): I'm on the bridge. I'm seeing increased queue depth on the dataplane pods in eu-west1. Control plane (console) shows all nodes healthy — could be a scheduling or config mismatch.

suhas (prod-ops): customer-facing: a handful of customers reported timeouts ~10:05 UTC. I've notified support. No broad outage but some 5xxs in the edge logs.

kevin (eng-sre): please paste logs and timeline here. we'll record hypotheses.

maria (oncall): timeline so far:
- 10:02 UTC: synthetic check triggers first latency alert.
- 10:04 UTC: on-call pages.
- 10:06 UTC: Support ticket from customer A reporting timeouts.
- 10:08 UTC: ops-bot reports elevated pod restart count in eu-west1.
- 10:11 UTC: we started additional logging, next steps set to mitigation.

ops-bot: Pod restarts observed:
```
pod/rt-gen-3c4f  restarted 3 times in last 5m
pod/kv-cache-7f2a restarted 2 times
node/gpu-12: kubelet OOM error at 10:05:18
```

olivia (eng-runtime): attaching a quick grep from dataplane logs (token masking removed):
```
2026-03-12T10:04:59Z ERROR serve: request timeout after queueing 120s
2026-03-12T10:05:03Z WARN kv-cache: eviction pressure high, free slots=2
2026-03-12T10:05:05Z INFO runtime: model loaded but failed to allocate kvcache: OutOfMemoryError
```

kevin (eng-sre): hypothesis 1: node-level OOM in eu-west1 caused kv-cache failures and cascading queueing. hypothesis 2: control-plane config (auto-scale policy) did not propagate, leaving less headroom. hypothesis 3: recent kernel-level driver bump on gpu node triggered instability.

maria (oncall): immediate mitigation: scale up dataplane replicas in eu-west1 by 30% and enable fallback to small-quantized model for burst routing. Olivia, can you push config?

olivia (eng-runtime): scaling now: `kubectl scale deployment rt-gen --replicas=13 -n prod-eu-west1` — starting new pods. Also enabling fallback route: updated runtime routing flags to prefer q4 models on latency>500ms.

ops-bot: Autoscaler event: manual scale to 13 replicas accepted at 10:12 UTC. New pods becoming ready.

suhas (prod-ops): alert to customers: posting an update to status page that we are seeing elevated latency in eu-west1 and working on mitigation.

kevin (eng-sre): collecting debug artifacts: please upload full pod logs and dmesg for node gpu-12. Also get kube events for last 30m.

olivia (eng-runtime): uploaded logs to /shared/incidents/1776504321/logs.tar.gz — includes pod logs, kube-events, and node dmesg. Key snippet shows `oom_kill` around 10:05:17 on gpu-12.

maria (oncall): handoff note for next oncall (kevin): we've enabled scaling and fallback routing. Still watching for errors. If latency persists after 10:22 UTC, escalate to infra (driver rollback).

kevin (eng-sre): got it. I'm going to run quick grep across logs to validate whether control-plane push failures occurred.

kevin (eng-sre): quick check: control-plane config push timeline shows a successful rollout at 09:55 UTC of `runtime.route.prefers_quantized=false` in eu-west1, then a later change at 10:00 UTC toggled `auto_scale.max_pods=12` (should have propagated). But dataplane nodes show `max_pods=8` in their local config at 10:04 UTC — suggests propagation lag.

maria (oncall): so combination: node OOM + config propagation lag + autoscaler limit => queueing. Sounds right.

olivia (eng-runtime): adding hypothesis 4: model hot-cache invalidation due to recent model reload at 09:58 UTC made kv-cache spikes. The model reload logs show `reload complete` at 09:59 but followed by many cache misses.

kevin (eng-sre): plan for RCA list in-thread:
- Gather full node dmesg, kube events, and control-plane push logs (assigned: olivia)
- Correlate time series: pod restarts, queue depth, control-plane push latency (assigned: kevin)
- Customer impact map (which tenants hit, % errors) (assigned: suhas)
- Verify if driver/kernel bump happened recently on images (assigned: infra after-hours)

suhas (prod-ops): customer impact so far: 7 customers affected, top 3 enterprise tenants saw 4-7% error rates over 6 minutes. Logging a post to the support thread with mitigation steps and ETA.

maria (oncall): note for post-incident: ensure control-plane rollout has stronger verification for datasync to dataplane (maybe a push confirmation).

kevin (eng-sre): current status: latency trending down after new pods ready at 10:15 UTC and fallback routing in place. We'll keep this thread for RCA and attach artifacts. If it reoccurs, re-open Sev2.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated (partial) at 10:18 UTC.

olivia (eng-runtime): uploading timeline and hypothesis doc to /shared/incidents/1776504321/timeline.md — includes per-pod logs and a short reproduction script.

maria (oncall): handoff: I'm signing out at 10:20 UTC, Kevin you're primary for RCA. Tag me for review of the postmortem. :thumbsup:

kevin (eng-sre): acknowledged, will own RCA and follow up with infra on driver check. Adding a watch for similar spikes across other regions.

suhas (prod-ops): closing loop with support: status page updated 10:19 UTC with mitigation note. I'll prepare a customer follow-up template for affected tenants.

maria (oncall): thanks all, I'll update the incident channel with the postmortem link once Kevin publishes.
